extracted.intended_audience: students, playwrights, and scholars of drama/literary theory
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for composing or evaluating tragic drama according to Aristotle's Poetics, emphasizing the six elements of tragedy, plot quality standards, and key dramatic concepts like catharsis, hamartia, peripeteia, and anagnorisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot (Mythos)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'organization of incidents.' The soul of tragedy. Should imitate an action evoking pity and fear. Plot transitions characters from good to bad fortune (or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex plots (involving reversal and recognition) are superior to simple plots; plot is the central element of tragedy and should drive emotional effects (pity and fear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Character (Ethos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must be good, appropriate, and consistent; they reveal themselves through actions and choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: be 'Good' (between moral extremes), 'Appropriate' (matching age, station, gender), and 'Consistent' (or 'consistently inconsistent' if change is properly explained). Character is valued insofar as it supports the plot and elicits pity/terror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought (Dianoia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'spoken reasoning' of characters: how they articulate ideas, motives, and arguments through dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thought should express and justify motives and themes; it is the logical and argumentative content of speeches that furthers the action and reveals character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction (Lexis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of speech and word choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speeches should reflect character and express meaning clearly; diction is evaluated by appropriateness of language to character and effectiveness in conveying the action's meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody (Melos)
rubrics_metrics.description: The musical/choreographic dimension; the chorus as an integrated character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Melody is the poetic and musical element that should contribute to the unity and emotional effect of the tragedy; the chorus functions as part of dramatic action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectacle (Opsis)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristotle regards spectacle as the least connected to the playwright's craft; it can affect impressions but is subordinate to plot and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimesis (Imitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation/representation/expression of action; the fundamental nature of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All art imitates; in tragedy imitation is of serious action and should produce the appropriate emotional response through representation rather than narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catharsis (Emotional Purging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purgation, purification, or clarification of the emotions of pity and terror experienced by spectators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful tragedy accomplishes catharsis—evoking pity and fear so that these emotions are clarified or purified in the audience; catharsis is the primary emotional aim of tragedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamartia (Tragic Error)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Miscalculation' or tragic error — a good character pushed toward undeserved misfortune through a mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hamartia explains how a deserving or 'good' character experiences fall; the error should be intelligible and connected to character and circumstance, eliciting pity rather than scorn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peripeteia (Reversal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reversal of fortune within the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peripeteia is a structural device where the action turns in an unexpected but necessary way; when combined with recognition it heightens the tragedy and supports catharsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anagnorisis (Recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition or identification — the moment when ignorance turns to knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anagnorisis often accompanies peripeteia in complex plots and reinforces the moral/causal logic of the reversal, increasing the emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness (Plot requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must have beginning, middle, and end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action should be whole and self-contained so the sequence of events forms a coherent, complete structure rather than a loose collection of episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude (Plot requirement)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action should be of a proper size or importance to produce the intended emotional response; too trivial or too vast scope can undercut effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity (Plot requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each event must follow logically from prior events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plot's incidents should be causally connected; unity requires that events arise from preceding circumstances and contribute to the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability and Necessity (Plot requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions must be plausible; even surprises must seem necessary in retrospect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though events can be unexpected, they must appear convincing and necessary when the whole action is considered; implausible events break the dramatic illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity (Plot requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex plots with reversals and recognitions are superior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plots that include peripeteia and anagnorisis (reversals and recognitions) produce stronger catharsis and are therefore higher quality than simple plots without these features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Representation of a serious, complete action of magnitude, in embellished speech... by people acting and not by narration, accomplishing through pity and terror the catharsis of such emotions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tragedy should be enacted rather than told, use elevated language suited to dramatic performance, and must combine seriousness, completeness, and emotional effect to achieve catharsis.
